body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Saturday, August 22, 2026, and our top story this morning is the arrest of a 15-year-old suspect in connection with the deadly shooting that occurred during Friday night’s Independence High School football game. We’re starting the day with a current temperature of 97° at Meadows Field, and we’re looking at a high near 103° later on. Air quality is moderate at AQI 64. Let’s take a look at what happened overnight across Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

The night’s most serious call came just after midnight, when a shooting was reported outside a Taco Bell in the Baker Street area. A witness told officers they saw someone shot, and the suspect was described as a white male in his 40s to 50s, wearing a black shirt and dark pants, sitting inside a white vehicle — possibly a Ford Explorer. Officers responded with an officer-safety broadcast. Earlier in the night, around 2:16 a.m., multiple engines and a truck company responded to a fire at a vacant single-story house on King Street, where flames were visible inside and heavy smoke was showing. The fire was under control by about 2:25. Just before 11 p.m., a two-vehicle collision near Gosford Road and Harris Road left one vehicle on fire. Engine 14 and Engine 9 responded to the scene, which was dubbed the Harris Incident, though injuries are unknown. Multiple reports of a grass fire along southbound Highway 395 north of Brown Road drew a large response — including engines, patrol units, a water tender, a dozer and a helicopter — but crews found a small roadside fire that was quickly extinguished, and the extra equipment was canceled. Around 10:38 p.m., an assault with a knife was reported with no injuries; the suspect, about 6 feet tall with neck tattoos and wearing black shorts, a gray shirt and white shoes, fled on foot northbound. Throughout the night, other incidents included a subject reported with a firearm in his waistband on Houchin Road around 10:04 p.m., an assault reported on Birch Avenue in Wasco around 11:22 p.m., a hit-and-run on Monterey Street involving a black Camry and a white sedan around 11:23 p.m., two fire hydrants spilling water on 22nd Street between Q and P streets around 11:53 p.m., a half acre burning behind a residence on Windsong Street around 12:01 a.m., a suspicious vehicle check on Culiacan Avenue around 12:09 a.m., a family disturbance on Suncrest Drive involving an intoxicated teenager around 12:10 a.m., and a welfare check on a man lying on the ground near the curb on 26th Street around 12:12 a.m.

## Today's weather

Today’s weather will bring a high near 103° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 97° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and there are no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at AQI 64. Be sure to stay hydrated and take precautions if you’ll be out in the heat today.

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that a deadly shooting at an Independence High School football game left nearby residents shaken, and a 15-year-old suspect was arrested miles away from the scene.** The scene at Independence High School was chaotic as people tried to understand what had happened after gunshots rang out nearby. A local resident, Erin Foster, described the unusual scene outside her home where the suspect was arrested, noting that a family remained outside for an extended period of time. Bakersfield Police Sgt. Eric Celedon acknowledged that while Friday night football games are generally safe, some community members may be hesitant to attend future games due to the incident.

**KGET 17 tells us that Bakersfield Mayor Karen Goh has released a statement addressing the deadly shooting at Independence High School.** In her statement, Mayor Goh expressed her condolences to the victim’s family and emphasized that the city is working closely with law enforcement to ensure the safety of all residents. She also urged anyone with information about the shooting to come forward and cooperate with the investigation.

**According to KGET 17, a 15-year-old has been arrested in connection to the deadly shooting at Independence High School.** The arrest was made following the incident that occurred during Friday night’s football game. Law enforcement officials are continuing their investigation into the matter.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Southwest Market has canceled its Saturday event at Independence High School following the fatal shooting.** Organizers of the event announced the cancellation on social media, citing the need to prioritize the safety and well-being of the community in light of the tragic incident.

**KGET 17 warns us about the dangers of flesh-eating bacteria and highlights the warning signs to watch out for.** The bacteria, which can lead to serious infections, often enter the body through open wounds or cuts. Symptoms to be aware of include redness, swelling, and pain at the infection site, as well as fever and chills. If you suspect you may have been exposed to flesh-eating bacteria, seek medical attention immediately.

## Something good

On a brighter note, a local family is hosting a Saturday flea market to raise funds for Villafana’s prosthetic leg. The event aims to collect $8,900 to support this important cause, and it’s a heartwarming example of our community coming together to help one of our own.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, there are several events and meetings on the calendar for this coming week. On Tuesday, August 26, the Bakersfield City Council will hold a Special City Council Meeting at 12:00 p.m., followed by a City Council Meeting at 3:30 p.m. and another at 5:15 p.m. Meanwhile, the Fox Theater has a busy schedule of performances, starting tonight with Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio. On Tuesday, August 26, you can catch Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027. Later in the week, Rodney Carrington will take the stage on Thursday, August 28, followed by CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on Friday, August 29. Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix will also perform at the Fox Theater on Saturday, August 30. Be sure to check out these events and mark your calendars accordingly.
